subject: Reserved capacity provisioning buffer and GPU-cost index clause — BrightLane
messages:
From: Harlan Brightlane <harlan@brightlane.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask + index clause question

Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the Dedicated offering looks like a strong fit for our payer inference workloads. Before we move to legal, procurement has one open item: BrightLane procurement prefers a price-index floor or short runway (12–18 months) to mitigate GPU market volatility.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide a worked example (NPV) showing how a 24-month commit with a 12-month index clause would look versus a fixed discount today? We care about downside protection if GPU spot/contract prices spike.
- Are there standard approval thresholds for tiered discounts that require manager or VP sign-off? If so, who should we expect to see looped in for a mid-size Reserved SKU ask (~1200 A100-equivalent hours/month)?

I attached the provisioning matrix BrightLane uses — happy to share more details if it helps.

Best,
Harlan
Procurement Lead, BrightLane Health
--
Attachment: provisioning_scenarios_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 96KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Harlan Brightlane <harlan@brightlane.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + index clause question

Harlan —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can model the NPV scenarios and we do have discount approval tiers (larger concessions need VP level). I’ve attached a concise SKU breakdown and a first-pass NPV table for the scenarios you described.

What I need from you to finalize:
- Confirm the 24-month preferred commit and the minimum monthly baseline for the runway (e.g., 70% of projected).
- Any hard constraints on contract language (index caps, lookback windows, or pass-through triggers).

Internal note: marissa — can you review the discount/approval ladder and confirm what level of discount for a 24-month, ~1200 A100-equivalent commit would require your sign-off vs. VP? If you can reply with the approver matrix and the default index-floor language we use, I’ll roll into the NPV.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + index clause question

Looping Kim for approvals & procurement ops guidance.

Karthik — rough guidance: for a deal with a committed monthly baseline ~1.2k A100-eq and 24 months, the typical discount band we can offer without exec escalation is up to midsize tier (we call it Tier B) — that's up to 18% off posted reserved unit price. Anything beyond 18% requires Director/VP approval. For index clauses, we usually accept a capped pass-through (up to X% per 6-month window) but require a carve-out that limits customer credits if price drops below a reference floor. That preserves economics if prices move down.

I’ll flag this to Finance but Kim — can you confirm whether a 12-month lookback & 15% cap is operationally clean? If so, we can present a formal option set to BrightLane (fixed-discount vs. index-floor-protected).

-Marissa
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + index clause question

Marissa / Karthik —

Finance and Legal runbook input below:
- 12-month lookback + 15% cap is acceptable from an operational standpoint. We will need a clause that defines the "price index" (we recommend published spot/contract blended price across top 3 cloud providers) and a quarterly reconciliation.
- Approval thresholds: Director sign-off for up to 18% discount; VP sign-off required for 18–24%; anything >24% is exec (CEO/CRO) level. Include an explicit fallback to on-demand or a pre-agreed substitute SKU in case of supply constraints.
- Please include a conservative provisioning buffer (we suggest +20% of baseline for peak months) in the provisioning schedule to reduce overage disputes.

I can pre-approve the standard index-floor template; if Karthik wants the 18% Tier B offer packaged, I can sign it and route to Legal for the clause language.

-Kim
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Harlan Brightlane <harlan@brightlane.ai>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + index clause question

Harlan —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the NPV comparison: (A) 24-month fixed discount at 16% (Tier B) vs (B) 24-month with a 12-month index floor and a 15% cap on upward pass-through. Key takeaways:
- With our provisioning buffer (+20% peak allowance) the fixed 16% looks slightly better if GPU contract prices remain flat; the index-floor option protects BrightLane from >10% sustained price shocks but increases expected cost by ~3–4% in our base model.
- Operationally we can accept the 12-month lookback & 15% cap. Kim has pre-approved Tier B (16%) discounts without VP escalation. Anything above 18% will require VP sign-off.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which pricing construct BrightLane prefers (Fixed 16% vs Index-floor 15% cap).
2) If Index-floor chosen, procurement/legal: confirm the index definition and sign DocuSign link.
3) If Fixed chosen and they accept Tier B, I will prepare the SOW and route to Marissa for signature.

I'll schedule a 30-min call if you want to walk through the NPV assumptions.

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
